content: The use of autologous hematopoietic stem cell-based gene therapy, specifically atidarsagene autotemcel, is indicated for the treatment of children with pre-symptomatic late infantile (PSLI), pre-symptomatic early juvenile (PSEJ), or early symptomatic early juvenile (ESEJ) metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD). This therapy is intended for autologous use only and is administered as a one-time, single-dose intravenous infusion. Prior to initiating conditioning, it is essential to confirm the availability and proper storage of atidarsagene autotemcel, as well as the availability of a back-up collection of CD34+ cells. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as abacavir, atazanavir, bictegravir, cabotegravir, didanosine, dolutegravir, doravirine, efavirenz, elvitegravir, emtricitabine, enfuvirtide, etravirine, fosamprenavir, indinavir, lamivudine, maraviroc, nelfinavir, and nevirapine, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Therefore, ARTs should not be taken for at least one month prior to cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for the elimination of these medications. The safety and effectiveness of vaccinations during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the start of myeloablative conditioning and should be avoided until hematologic recovery is achieved following treatment. If feasible, childhood vaccinations should be administered prior to initiating myeloablative conditioning. Specific vaccines, including live vaccines (e.g., adenovirus types 4 and 7, anthrax, BCG, chikungunya, dengue, measles-mumps-rubella, measles-mumps-rubella-varicella, influenza intranasal, and varicella), inactivated vaccines (e.g., hepatitis A, hepatitis B, Haemophilus influenzae type B, Japanese encephalitis, meningococcal, pneumococcal, and COVID-19 vaccines), and recombinant or adjuvanted vaccines (e.g., influenza recombinant, influenza adjuvanted, and COVID-19 adjuvanted), should be avoided or used with caution. The timing of vaccination should be carefully planned, and childhood vaccinations should ideally be completed before starting myeloablative conditioning.
